papers.title: Governance Invariant for Autonomous Systems
papers.claims_scope: Proposes a monotonic authority-contraction safety property for autonomous socio-technical systems under epistemic degradation.
known_limitations: Scalar notation may be inadequate for action-set semantics.
Emergency authority and authorized re-expansion require formal treatment.

papers.title: Survivable Governance
papers.claims_scope: Defines governance behavior intended to remain bounded when trust and historical reconstruction degrade.
known_limitations: Canonical full manuscript has not yet been reconstructed.
The framework bounds behavior rather than proving correctness.

papers.title: Formal Model Sketch: Survivable Governance Under Epistemic Constraint
papers.claims_scope: Defines a minimal state model over trust, boundary mode, and audit status with monotonic tightening under uncertainty.
known_limitations: State integrity and degraded enforcement capacity are not yet integrated.
Transition semantics and recovery conditions require formalization.

papers.title: Trust-Bounded Socio-Technical Systems: Architectural Primitives for Auditability and Failure
papers.claims_scope: Treats trust and irrecoverable audit loss as operational state and boundaries as execution mechanisms.
known_limitations: Canonical full manuscript has not yet been reconstructed.

papers.title: Ghost Credentials and Phantom Trust
papers.claims_scope: Identifies failure modes where credential validity or inherited trust persists after substantive justification disappears.
known_limitations: The failure modes require sharper differentiation from existing authorization and revocation literature.
The paper identifies uncertainty but does not eliminate it.

papers.title: Boundary-Condition Autonomy
papers.claims_scope: Treats autonomy as a revocable execution mode governed by enforceable boundary conditions at the state-transition boundary.
known_limitations: Does not solve alignment or ethics.
No executable reference model or formal proof is committed.
Relationship to external irreversibility frameworks requires primary-source verification.
